input.reasoning:
Backlog totals 81 story points across 8 tasks. With no historical actuals, I used a standard heuristic of ~6-8 hours of total delivery effort per story point (blended across dev/QA/devops/design), then allocated hours per task to roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, infra, QA, data migration). I cross-checked total allocated hours per role against available FTE capacity over an assumed ~12-week (3-month) delivery window (1 FTE ≈ 480 hours over 12 weeks at ~40% utilization on this project, i.e. ~160h/month per FTE if fully dedicated, but roles are shared so I capped allocations to realistic capacity).

Task-level breakdown (hours split across roles):
- PW-1 CI pipeline & staging (5 pts, High): DevOps-led, some Backend support.
- PW-2 Design system (8 pts, Medium): Frontend-led, light QA.
- PW-3 Registration/login (8 pts, Urgent): Backend + Frontend + QA, security-sensitive.
- PW-4 RBAC (13 pts, High): Backend-heavy with Frontend + QA, cross-cutting complexity.
- PW-5 Dashboard (8 pts, High): Frontend-led with Backend API support + QA.
- PW-6 Invoice list/detail (5 pts, Medium): Frontend + Backend (PDF gen) + QA.
- PW-7 Payment integration (13 pts, Urgent): Backend-heavy (Stripe, webhooks, reconciliation) + QA + some DevOps for webhook infra.
- PW-8 Legacy data migration (21 pts, High): Backend-heavy + DevOps for infra/cutover + QA for data validation; largest single task given its scale (400k records, 2M invoice lines).

Given QA (0.6 FTE) and DevOps (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed, I kept their hours proportionally lower than Backend/Frontend, noting risk of QA/DevOps being a bottleneck across concurrent high-priority urgent items (PW-3, PW-4, PW-7, PW-8 overlap in priority).

Non-labour costs include Stripe sandbox/test fees, staging cloud infrastructure, Oracle migration tooling/licensing, and a contingency buffer for the data migration task given its inherent uncertainty (schema quirks, data quality issues).

Scenarios: Base case at ~50th percentile reflects the estimate as broken down. A P75 "realistic-with-risk" scenario adds ~15% for RBAC/migration complexity and QA bottleneck risk. A P90 "conservative" scenario adds ~30% to cover legacy migration overruns (a common high-variance task) and payment integration compliance/edge cases.

scenarios.name: Optimistic (base plan, no major risks materialize)
Realistic (accounts for RBAC/migration complexity, QA bottleneck)
Conservative (legacy migration overrun, payment compliance edge cases)

nonLabourLines.description: Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (PW-1) setup and 3 months hosting
Stripe integration test/sandbox fees and PCI review support (PW-7)
Contingency buffer for legacy data migration data-quality issues (PW-8)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based on story-point-to-hour heuristics and task decomposition, not on measured team velocity.
Assumed ~6-8 effort-hours per story point on average, adjusted per task based on which roles are primarily involved.

Assumed a delivery window of roughly 10-14 weeks, during which QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are shared/thin resources and may bottleneck if urgent/high-priority tasks (PW-3, PW-4, PW-7, PW-8) run concurrently.

PW-8 (Legacy Data Migration, 21 points) is treated as the highest-risk task given its scale (400k customer records, 2M invoice lines) and is given a non-labour contingency buffer in addition to labour hours.
Non-labour costs are estimates for infrastructure, third-party tooling, and Stripe-related sandbox/compliance support; no vendor quotes were provided so these are indicative.

Backend Developer hours (620h) are within capacity for 1.5 FTE over the assumed window; Frontend Developer hours (420h) are within capacity for 1.0 FTE; QA and DevOps hours are kept conservative relative to their smaller FTE allocations to avoid overcommitting thinly staffed roles.

RBAC (PW-4) and Payment Integration (PW-7) are assumed to require the most cross-functional coordination (Backend+Frontend+QA), reflected in higher blended hours per point than simpler tasks like PW-6.
Priority breakdown totals are labour-cost only, allocated pro-rata to each task's priority; non-labour costs are shown separately as they are not attributable to a single priority tier.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal 'buttons + forms + tables' set now, defer full theming tokens and dialogs to a later phase
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~95h on PW-2; theming/dialogs delivered in a follow-up iteration

reductions.description: Defer PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view) to next release since it is Medium priority and not required for initial launch
reductions.effect: Removes all labour hours allocated to PW-6 (Backend, Frontend, QA) from this phase's scope

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer hours on lower-risk tasks (PW-2, PW-6) by relying on Frontend/Backend developers for initial testing and reserving dedicated QA for Urgent items (PW-3, PW-7) and PW-8 data validation
reductions.effect: Cuts ~60 QA hours from Medium-priority tasks, reallocating QA capacity to higher-risk urgent work instead of adding scope

reductions.description: Use a managed migration service/off-the-shelf ETL tool instead of custom-built scripts for PW-8, reducing Backend Developer hours needed for migration tooling
reductions.effect: Cuts ~100 Backend Developer hours on PW-8 by leveraging existing tooling rather than building custom migration code

reductions.description: Defer non-critical Stripe reconciliation reporting features in PW-7 to a post-launch iteration, keeping only core payment + webhook handling for go-live
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer and QA hours on PW-7 by narrowing initial scope to payment processing and essential webhooks only
